subject.title: Feature: Multi-index embedding memory with model-aware failover (no mixed vector spaces)

question: Should OpenClaw add first-class multi-index memorySearch config, storage, ingestion, status, and failover routing in memory-core, or keep core on the current single-index model while only fixing narrower fallback recovery bugs?
rationale: The request is valid but crosses product API, config compatibility, persistent storage, provider-routing, observability, and doctor migration boundaries that automation should not choose unilaterally.

options.title: Approve multi-index design
options.body: Define an additive memory-core config/storage/status API with explicit doctor migration and upgrade behavior before implementation.

options.title: Limit to narrow bug fixes
options.body: Keep this design issue open but only queue bounded repairs such as provider fallback recovery until maintainers approve the broader API.

options.title: Reject core feature for now
options.body: Decline multi-index core work and ask for a plugin/API proposal only if current plugin seams are insufficient.

recommendation.title: Approve multi-index design
recommendation.body: Define an additive memory-core config/storage/status API with explicit doctor migration and upgrade behavior before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: osolmaz is assigned on the live issue and has recent history in the memory provider failure/fallback path this design would change.
